messages:
Jordan Yang: Hey @people-ops — heads up: I'm planning to relocate to Tokyo (permanent) in ~6 weeks. Need clarity on payroll cutover, local benefits (health/pension), any tax/nexus risk for Redwood, and how WFH stipend vs coworking reimbursement will work. What's the process and ETA?
Mei Chen: Congrats, Jordan! Quick top-level: we can support a Japan-based employee but it's not instant. Main things: payroll vendor onboarding, local bank account, social insurance enrollment (Shakai Hoken) if you remain an employee, and immigration status affects options. Nexus: single headcount usually low risk for PE but need legal check. Can you confirm visa type and whether you'll be on a local contract or remain on US payroll?
Jordan Yang: I'll be on my spouse visa (work permitted) and want to stay on Redwood's employment terms if possible. Prefer to stay on company payroll rather than 1099.
Arjun Patel: From legal/tax perspective: spouse visa + working activities = employee in JP. One employee typically won't create a permanent establishment by itself, but if Jordan will be doing sales/contract negotiation, that ups the risk. I'll run a quick memo and loop in our tax counsel.
Rachel Ortiz: Payroll notes: we use "GlobalPayroll" (our vendor) for Japan. Typical onboarding 30–45 days: need Japanese address, bank (Zengin), copy of visa, passport, and a signed local payroll adendum if moving onto local payroll. If you stay on US payroll, benefits handling and tax withholding are more complex.
Rachel Ortiz: Stipend details: WFH stipend proration = monthly. Coworking reimbursement: submit receipts up to 15,000 JPY/month (pre-approval required). Relocation one-time allowance is separate — submit relocation request.
Mei Chen: Practical checklist (so we don't forget):
```
- Confirm visa type + copy of visa/passport (Jordan)  
- Decide payroll model: keep US payroll (expensed tax advice) OR transition to JP payroll (recommended)  
- Submit local address + bank details (Jordan)  
- People Ops: open payroll onboarding with GlobalPayroll (Rachel)  
- Legal/Tax: PE review + RSU/withholding impact (Arjun)  
- Benefits: enroll in statutory health/pension or opt for private top-up (Mei/Rachel)  
- Stipend: set coworking cap and proration date (People Ops)  
```
Jordan Yang: Thanks. If I transition to JP payroll, what happens to my US health insurance and 401(k)?
Rachel Ortiz: If on JP payroll we typically offboard US medical and 401(k) plan participation (can't continue on US plan if not US-base). We enroll in Japanese statutory health and pension (employer contribution applies). We can discuss 401(k) rollover options with Benefits.
Arjun Patel: Also flagged: equity/RSU tax withholding differs by jurisdiction. We'll need to run a simulation for net pay. People-ops-bot: Note created: relocation-case-1767123456, linking comp/benefits for RSU tax check.
payroll-bot: Payroll ticket PR-5234 created for Jordan Yang — Japan onboarding. Estimated vendor ETA: 35 days. Required docs: passport, visa, JP address, JP bank. Upload link: https://payroll.internal/upload/PR-5234
Mei Chen: Timeline summary: if Jordan provides docs within 7 days and signs local adendum, likely timeline: vendor onboarding 30–45 days, first JP payroll run next calendar month after cutover. If missed payroll cutoff this month, fallback is next month.
Jordan Yang: Got it. I'll gather visa, bank, and address tonight and submit. One more Q: does this trigger any team coverage changes (timezone expectations)?
Mei Chen: Team Ops note: please coordinate with your manager on on-call / meeting expectations — Japan is +13/+14 UTC depending DST. We can mark your timezone in Slack and adjust rotation.
Rachel Ortiz: I'll start the onboarding ticket now. Jordan, please fill the short form at: https://forms.internal/relocate-jp and upload docs to the payroll link.
Jordan Yang: Done — submitted the form and uploaded passport + visa. Thanks all.
Mei Chen: Thanks — looping in Arjun and Payroll for next steps. Will update this thread when vendor confirms start date. :rocket:
